newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close firmer despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close firmer despite profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished higher on Saturday for the second straight day despite profit-taking which emerged at mid-session to erode sharp early gains, brokers said.

The weighted index ended a scant 0.33 percent or 23.30 points higher at 7,118.07 after hitting an intra-session high of 7,178.18 at the open. Turnover in the abbreviated Saturday session was a heavy T$85.92 billion.
Brokers attributed early sharp rises to bullish buying following Friday's 1.2 percent gain and Wall Street's overnight rebound.
But the market lost steam as the index approached the strong 7,200-point resistance, brokers said.
"Many people decide to slow their pace as the index moves towards the 7,200 points barrier," said Lin Long-hsien, an analyst of United Securities.
Saturday's gainers were plastics and textiles, which rose 1.16 percent and 1.18 percent, respectively.
The most active issue was Pacific Wire and Cable, up 50 cents or 1.87 percent to T$27.2, followed by China Development Corp, which gained T$2 or 2.33 percent to T$88.
Brokers said they were optimistic that the market will soon test resistance at 7,200 points.
"With liquidity continuing to flow into the stock market and the government's supportive attitude, the market is in an uptrend," Lin said.
"It won't take long to breach the resistance level."
A 7,000-7,200 trading range was seen for next week.
